title: Horizontal Drainage Fitting Selection: Wyes vs. Sanitary Tees
description: Using a standard sanitary tee on a horizontal-to-horizontal drainage run is a common installation mistake that causes frequent clogs and poor flow velocity. Sanitary tees are designed primarily for transitioning from horizontal to vertical flow. On horizontal runs, horizontal-to-horizontal changes in direction require a combination wye and 1/8 bend or a long-sweep fitting. This allows wastewater and solid matter to sweep smoothly into the main branch without splashing back, maintaining proper hydraulic flow and preventing solid buildup over time. Always consult local plumbing code requirements for approved fitting orientations on horizontal drain lines.

Horizontal Drainage Fitting Selection: Wyes vs. Sanitary Tees

Using a standard sanitary tee on a horizontal-to-horizontal drainage run is a common installation mistake that causes frequent clogs and poor flow velocity. Sanitary tees are designed primarily for transitioning from horizontal to vertical flow. On horizontal runs, horizontal-to-horizontal changes in direction require a combination wye and 1/8 bend or a long-sweep fitting. This allows wastewater and solid matter to sweep smoothly into the main branch without splashing back, maintaining proper hydraulic flow and preventing solid buildup over time. Always consult local plumbing code requirements for approved fitting orientations on horizontal drain lines.
